JUDGMENT Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming compensation amount of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
That on 13.10.2024, she along with her husband and daughter were traveling in a KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2261 from Kukke subramanya to Bangalore, the driver of the said bus drove the vehicle with high speed rash and negligent manner and he has negligently cross the road hump near Navayuga Toll, Nelamangala, as a Shanthamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4440030/
1 result, petitioner who was sitting at the left side of the back seat, window side, she suddenly fall on the iron rod of the bus, and sustained grievous injuries, she was shifted to Suguna Hospital for first aid, later she was shifted to Nandi Hospital,
Bangalore and Sarojini Hospital, Bangalore wherein she took treatment as inpatient for accidental injuries and she has spent Rs.10,00,000/- towards her medical expenses.
She stated that due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to perform her work as earlier.
Prior to the accident the she was hale and healthy and she is aged about 34 years and she was working as Nursery worker/ construction labour and thereby she was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further petitioner stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to respondent and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.416/2024 against the driver of the offending KSRTC bus.
She prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondent, he appeared through their/its counsel and filed vakalath, written statement by denying the entire version of the petitioner in toto.

Respondent specifically denied the age, income and profession of the petitioner and contended that the petitioner had sustained injuries due to her own negligent act and prays this Tribunal to dismiss the petition.
4.
Petitioner examined herself as PW-3 and examined medical record department official and doctor as PW.1 & 2 and got marked 24 documents, which are at Ex.P.1 to 24 and they are fully cross examined.
Respondent examined the driver of the KSRTC bus as RW-1 and he is fully cross examined.
5. I have heard the arguments for the counsel appearing for both the sides and I have perused the entire records.

6. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 13.10.2024, she along with her husband and daughter were traveling in a KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2261 from Kukke subramanya to Bangalore, the driver of the said bus was driving the vehicle with high speed rash and negligent manner and he has negligently cross the road hump near Navayuga Toll, Nelamangala, as a result, petitioner who was sitting at the left side of the back seat, window side, she suddenly fall on the iron rod of the bus, and sustained grievous injuries due to the negligent act of the driver of the bus as alleged in the petition?
2.Whether respondent proves that the petitioner has sustained injuries due to her own negligent act as contended at para No.9 of the written statement ?
Shanthamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4440030/
2
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4. What order or award?
PW1 being the petitioner, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of complaint, FIR, mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and final report, police intimation, MLC register which are at Ex.P.9 to 14,
17, 2 & 3.
9.

On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one V.S.Bore gowda S/o late Sidde gowda was the driver of the offending KSRTC bus and the accident took place due to his rash and negligent act.
Ex . P.16
reply notice given by respondent wherein they admit that VS Bore Gowda was the driver of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.

Wound certificate,
Discharge summaries Ex.P.14, 19 reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries that is burst fracture of L1 vertebral body with Retropulsion of Frament causing spinal canal stenosis,
fractures fragment causing compression of conus, spinal cord oedema L4/5 disc prolapse causing bilateral nerve root compression and disc fixation was done on 13.10.2024 and she has taken treatment for 15 days as an inpatient and she has spent Rs.9,24,043/- as per Ex.P.20, 21.
10.
In the cross examination of the PW-3 she clearly denied the suggestion that she sustained injuries due to her negligent act.
Nothing worth has been elicited from the mouth of the PW-3 to disprove her version and to probabilise their contention as contended in the written statement.
Respondent has not denied the alleged accident and the involvement of the offending KSRTC bus and negligent act of the driver.
Respondent has admitted the final report which is at Ex.

P.17. 
Respondent has not chosen to examine the IO of this case, nor challenged the final report which is at Ex.P.17.
Final report is filed after through investigation and it cannot be brush aside.
Inasmuch respondent version cannot accepted without any tantamount evidence.

11. Admittedly she has taken treatment as an inpatient for 15 days, for attendant charges,
transportation, nourishing food, she might have spent some more expenses.
Therefore, in addition actual medical expenses of Rs.9,24,043/-, I award Rs.20,000/- and petitioner is entitled for Rs.9,44,043/-, compensation under this head.

Shanthamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4440030/
3
Loss of income during laid up period.
12. The petitioner has not substantiated her nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place in the year 2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as her monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least two months, she has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.33,000/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
13. The petitioner has examined the doctor Veeresha U Mathad, working as senior consultant neurosurgeon at Manipal Hospital, Sarjapura Road, Bangalore as PW-2.
He admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and he has verified the wound certificate, discharge summaries.

He deposed that, petitioner has sustained spinal card injury and paraplegia and she is bed ridden and she is not able to do any work and she has to depend on other for her daily living and she need a wheel chair and attainder to assist her during her life time.
He further deposed that she has no control over urine stools.
She has lost her sensation below the waist.
He further clarified that petitioner is having permanent severe neurological disability of 61% and she has 100% functional disability.
In the cross examination of PW-2, nothing worth is elicited to disbelieve the accidental injuries of the petitioners and the permanent functional disability assessed by PW-2.
The oral testimony of PW-2 corroborates with wound certificate discharge summary, CT scan reports, X-rays.
Learned counsel for the respondent argued that the assessment of PW-2 is on higher side.
Evidently petitioner has not examined the doctor who has treated her.

Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of PW-2, the assessment of permanent physical disability and functional disability of the petitioner cannot be doubted, accordingly the functional disability is assessed as 100%.
14. The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.16,500/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 34 years as per the entry in Aadhar card which is at Ex P.18.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "16".
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.31,68,000/- as compensation under this head.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
15.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, and during her life time she has to undergone lot of pain and sufferings.
Therefore I award Rs.2,00,000/- under this head.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
Shanthamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4440030/
4 16.
The petitioner has to forgone certain amenities available for her.
Therefore I award Rs.1,00,000/- as compensation under this head.

As per the oral testimony of PW-2, petitioner is in need of a helper/ attainder during her life time and she need wheel chair and she has lost her marital bliss which cannot compensated in terms of money.
Petitioner has not placed estimated cost of the wheel chair and cost of servant.
Accordingly she is entitled for tentative cost of wheel chair of Rs.20,000/- and lump sum cost of the labour Rs.3,00,000/- and Rs.5,00,000/- towards loss of marital bliss considering her age.
17. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.

In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
SN Particulars Amount  1

Towards medical expenses, attendant Rs. 9,44,043/-
charges, transportation, nourishing food 2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 33,000/- 3 Loss of income on account of Rs.31.68.000/- permanent functional disability 4 pain & sufferings Rs.
2.00,000/-
5 loss of amenities Rs. 1.00,000/-
6 Tentative cost of wheel chair Rs. 20,000/- 7
Lump sum cost of labour Rs. 3,00,000/- 8 Loss of Marital bliss Rs. 5,00,000/-
Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% P.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.a. on the compensation amount.
19. Liability :
As per the police records the accident took place due the sole rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which belongs to Respondent.
It is not disputed that the respondent is the insurer of the said offending vehicle which caused the accident and the validity of the said policy is not disputed.
Accordingly respondent is liable and has to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly respondent is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.
Accordingly I am answering issue no.1 in the affirmative, issue no.2 in the negative and issue no.3 in partly affirmative.
20. Issue No.4; For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.

Shanthamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4440030/
5
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.52,65,043/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.a. from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, Cash sheristedar is directed to release the 75% of the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020.
Further balance compensation amount of 25%, shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in a nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
Issue intimation to the banker not to allow the petitioner to create encumbrance on her deposited amount and not to permit her for premature withdrawal of the deposit amount.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
